Data Cleaning & EDA — Geotechnical UCS Dataset

Goal: Take a messy laboratory export of rock-core tests and turn it into a clean, trustworthy dataset, then explore what controls Uniaxial Compressive Strength (UCS).

Dataset: ucs_raw_dirty.csv, a synthetic dataset of ~650 rock-core tests from 8 boreholes.

Workflow:

  1. Load & first look
  2. Data-quality audit
  3. Cleaning (step by step)
  4. Exploratory Data Analysis
  5. Findings & next steps

Abstract

This study presents a complete data cleaning and exploratory data analysis workflow applied to a synthetic dataset of 650 rock-core tests measuring Uniaxial Compressive Strength (UCS). The dataset was intentionally corrupted with 13 types of realistic data-quality issues — placeholders, unit mixing, duplicates, mixed date formats, spelling inconsistencies, and physically impossible values.

The cleaning process reduced the dataset from 670 raw rows to a validated subset, with every change logged. Exploratory analysis confirmed that rock type and weathering grade are the dominant controls on UCS, while saturation weakens shale and mudstone most significantly — visible only after controlling for weathering. The Is(50) point load test emerged as the strongest predictor (ρ = 0.97 with UCS).

Keywords: Data cleaning, UCS, rock mechanics, exploratory data analysis, Spearman correlation, weathering

2. Dataset Generation

A synthetic dataset of 650 rock-core tests was generated with 21 columns, covering:

Category Columns
Location Sample ID, Borehole, Depth
Geology Rock Type, Weathering Grade
Test condition Moisture Condition
Geometry Core Diameter, L/D Ratio
Index properties Dry Density, Porosity, Water Content
Other indicators P-wave Velocity, Schmidt Rebound, Is(50), BTS
Target UCS, UCS Unit
Metadata Failure Mode, Test Date, Lab

Realistic relationships built-in:

  • UCS = rock type base × weathering multiplier × noise
  • Is(50) ≈ UCS / 20
  • Porosity, Vp, Schmidt R, BTS all correlated with UCS

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

np.random.seed(42)

n = 650

rock_types = ["Sandstone", "Limestone", "Shale", "Granite", "Mudstone", "Basalt"]
boreholes = [f"BH-{i:02d}" for i in range(1, 9)]
labs = ["Lab-A", "Lab-B", "Lab-C", "Lab-D"]

# ==================================================================
# REALISTIC RELATIONSHIPS — Rock type base + Weathering multiplier
# ==================================================================
rock_base_ucs = {
    "Mudstone":  15, "Shale": 25, "Sandstone": 50,
    "Limestone": 55, "Granite": 100, "Basalt": 140,
}

weather_mult = {
    "Fresh":                 1.00,
    "Slightly Weathered":    0.72,
    "Moderately Weathered":  0.45,
    "Highly Weathered":      0.22,
    "Completely Weathered":  0.08,
}

# ==================================================================
# BASE DATA
# ==================================================================
data = {
    "Sample ID": [f"S{5000+i}" for i in range(n)],
    "Borehole":  np.random.choice(boreholes, n),
    "Depth (m)": np.round(np.random.uniform(0.4, 65, n), 2),
    "Rock Type": np.random.choice(rock_types, n),
    "Weathering Grade": np.random.choice(
        ["Fresh", "Slightly Weathered", "Moderately Weathered",
         "Highly Weathered", "Completely Weathered"],
        n, p=[.28, .27, .22, .15, .08]),
    "Moisture Condition": np.random.choice(["Dry", "As received", "Saturated"],
                                            n, p=[.4, .4, .2]),
    "Core Diameter (mm)": np.random.choice([54, 63.5, 75, 85], n),
    "L/D Ratio": np.round(np.random.uniform(1.5, 2.9, n), 2),
    "Dry Density (g/cm3)": np.round(np.random.uniform(1.4, 2.95, n), 3),
    "Water Content (%)": np.round(np.random.uniform(0.1, 16, n), 2),
    "UCS Unit": np.random.choice(["MPa", "Pa", "ksi", "kgf/cm2"], n,
                                  p=[.75, .12, .08, .05]),
    "Failure Mode": np.random.choice(
        ["Axial splitting", "Single shear", "Multiple fractures",
         "Failure along joint", "Failed outside specimen body"], n),
    "Test Date": [f"2024-{np.random.randint(1,13):02d}-{np.random.randint(1,28):02d}"
                  for _ in range(n)],
    "Lab": np.random.choice(labs, n, p=[.3, .35, .2, .15]),
}

raw = pd.DataFrame(data)

# ==================================================================
# REALISTIC UCS — rock × weathering × noise
# ==================================================================
base = raw["Rock Type"].map(rock_base_ucs).values
wmul = raw["Weathering Grade"].map(weather_mult).values
noise = np.random.uniform(0.75, 1.30, n)
raw["UCS"] = np.round(base * wmul * noise, 2)

ucs_vals = raw["UCS"].values

# ==================================================================
# RELATED PREDICTORS — UCS se linked
# ==================================================================
# Is(50): UCS / ~20 (k ~ 20)
raw["Is(50) (MPa)"] = np.round(
    ucs_vals / 20 * np.random.uniform(0.7, 1.3, n), 2)

# P-wave velocity: log relation with UCS
raw["P-wave Velocity (km/s)"] = np.round(
    1.8 + 2.5 * np.log10(ucs_vals + 1) + np.random.normal(0, 0.4, n), 2)

# Schmidt Rebound: log relation
raw["Schmidt Rebound (R)"] = np.round(
    15 + 20 * np.log10(ucs_vals + 1) + np.random.normal(0, 4, n), 1)

# Porosity: negative log relation
raw["Porosity (%)"] = np.round(
    35 - 8 * np.log10(ucs_vals + 1) + np.random.normal(0, 4, n), 2)

# BTS: ~ UCS / 10
raw["Brazilian Tensile (MPa)"] = np.round(
    ucs_vals / 10 * np.random.uniform(0.6, 1.4, n), 2)

# Clamp realistic ranges
raw["P-wave Velocity (km/s)"]  = raw["P-wave Velocity (km/s)"].clip(1.0, 6.8)
raw["Schmidt Rebound (R)"]     = raw["Schmidt Rebound (R)"].clip(8, 72)
raw["Porosity (%)"]             = raw["Porosity (%)"].clip(0.3, 45)
raw["Is(50) (MPa)"]            = raw["Is(50) (MPa)"].clip(0.05, 15)
raw["Brazilian Tensile (MPa)"] = raw["Brazilian Tensile (MPa)"].clip(0.05, 30)

# Column order (original jaisa)
raw = raw[["Sample ID", "Borehole", "Depth (m)", "Rock Type", "Weathering Grade",
           "Moisture Condition", "Core Diameter (mm)", "L/D Ratio",
           "Dry Density (g/cm3)", "Porosity (%)", "Water Content (%)",
           "P-wave Velocity (km/s)", "Schmidt Rebound (R)", "Is(50) (MPa)",
           "Brazilian Tensile (MPa)", "UCS", "UCS Unit", "Failure Mode",
           "Test Date", "Lab"]]

# Object dtype banao (errors inject karne ke liye)
raw = raw.astype({c: "object" for c in raw.columns})


# ==================================================================
# ERROR 2: Placeholder tokens
# ==================================================================
idx = np.random.choice(n, 55, replace=False)
raw.loc[idx[0:12],  "Porosity (%)"]           = "NIL"
raw.loc[idx[12:23], "Water Content (%)"]      = "#N/A"
raw.loc[idx[23:34], "P-wave Velocity (km/s)"] = "void"
raw.loc[idx[34:44], "Schmidt Rebound (R)"]    = -777
raw.loc[idx[44:55], "Is(50) (MPa)"]           = "..."


# ==================================================================
# ERROR 3: Conflicting duplicates
# ==================================================================
dup_ids  = raw.sample(20, random_state=5)["Sample ID"].values
dup_rows = raw[raw["Sample ID"].isin(dup_ids)].copy()
dup_rows["UCS"] = (pd.to_numeric(dup_rows["UCS"], errors="coerce") *
                    np.random.uniform(0.55, 1.5, len(dup_rows))).round(2)
raw = pd.concat([raw, dup_rows], ignore_index=True)
print("Added", len(dup_rows), "conflicting duplicate rows")


# ==================================================================
# ERROR 4: Units inside TEXT columns
# ==================================================================
idx = np.random.choice(len(raw), 45, replace=False)

diam_vals = raw.loc[idx[:22], "Core Diameter (mm)"].astype(str) + " mm"
raw.loc[idx[:22], "Core Diameter (mm)"] = diam_vals.values

dens_vals = (pd.to_numeric(raw.loc[idx[22:45], "Dry Density (g/cm3)"], errors="coerce")
              * 1000).round(0).astype(int).astype(str) + " kg/m3"
raw.loc[idx[22:45], "Dry Density (g/cm3)"] = dens_vals.values


# ==================================================================
# ERROR 5: Rock type spelling
# ==================================================================
spelling_map = {
    "Sandstone":  ["Sand-Stone", "SS", "sandst", "SAND-STN"],
    "Limestone":  ["LIMEst.", "Lime Stone", "LS", "limest"],
    "Shale":      ["SHALE", "Shl", "Sh.", "shale"],
    "Granite":    ["granit.", "GRAN", "Grnt", "granite"],
    "Mudstone":   ["Md stone", "MUDST", "Mud St.", "mudstone"],
    "Basalt":     ["BSLT", "Bas.", "baslt", "BASALT"],
}
for orig, variants in spelling_map.items():
    mask = raw["Rock Type"] == orig
    change_mask = mask & (np.random.rand(len(raw)) < 0.18)
    if change_mask.any():
        raw.loc[change_mask, "Rock Type"] = np.random.choice(variants, change_mask.sum())


# ==================================================================
# ERROR 6: Weathering in 5 different systems
# ==================================================================
idx = np.random.choice(len(raw), int(0.4*len(raw)), replace=False)
weather_variants = {
    "Fresh":                 ["F", "Grade-1", "W1", "FR"],
    "Slightly Weathered":    ["SW", "Grade-2", "W2", "slgt-wthrd"],
    "Moderately Weathered":  ["MW", "Grade-3", "W3"],
    "Highly Weathered":      ["HW", "Grade-4", "W4"],
    "Completely Weathered":  ["CW", "Grade-5", "W5"],
}
for i in idx:
    orig = raw.loc[i, "Weathering Grade"]
    if orig in weather_variants:
        raw.loc[i, "Weathering Grade"] = np.random.choice(weather_variants[orig])


# ==================================================================
# ERROR 7: Target unit mixing (Pa / ksi / kgf/cm2)
# ==================================================================
def convert_ucs(row):
    v = pd.to_numeric(row["UCS"], errors="coerce")
    u = row["UCS Unit"]
    if pd.isna(v):   return np.nan
    if u == "Pa":        return v * 1_000_000
    if u == "ksi":       return v * 0.145038
    if u == "kgf/cm2":   return v * 10.1972
    return v
raw["UCS"] = raw.apply(convert_ucs, axis=1)


# ==================================================================
# ERROR 8: Density in lb/ft³ for some rows
# ==================================================================
idx = np.random.choice(len(raw), 28, replace=False)

def to_gcm3(x):
    s = str(x).replace(" kg/m3", "").strip()
    try:
        v = float(s)
    except:
        return np.nan
    if v > 100:
        return v / 1000
    return v

gcm3_vals = raw.loc[idx, "Dry Density (g/cm3)"].apply(to_gcm3)
raw.loc[idx, "Dry Density (g/cm3)"] = (gcm3_vals * 62.42796).round(1).values


# ==================================================================
# ERROR 9: Physically impossible
# ==================================================================
idx = np.random.choice(len(raw), 18, replace=False)
raw.loc[idx[0:4],  "Depth (m)"]                = [-4.5, -12.3, 850, -0.9]
raw.loc[idx[4:7],  "Porosity (%)"]             = [245, 178, 132]
raw.loc[idx[7:10], "UCS"]                      = [-8.4, -15.2, -3.6]
raw.loc[idx[10:12],"Schmidt Rebound (R)"]      = [150, 220]
raw.loc[idx[12:14],"P-wave Velocity (km/s)"]   = [22.5, -3.1]
raw.loc[idx[14:16],"Water Content (%)"]        = [-2.5, 68]
raw.loc[idx[16:18],"L/D Ratio"]                = [0.4, 5.6]


# ==================================================================
# ERROR 10: Invalid tests
# ==================================================================
ld_num = pd.to_numeric(raw["L/D Ratio"], errors="coerce")
raw["valid_test"] = ~(
    (ld_num > 3.0)
    | (raw["Failure Mode"] == "Failed outside specimen body")
)
print("Invalid tests to flag:", (~raw["valid_test"]).sum())


# ==================================================================
# ERROR 11: Mixed date formats
# ==================================================================
raw["Test Date"] = raw["Test Date"].apply(
    lambda d: np.random.choice([
        pd.to_datetime(d).strftime("%b-%d-%Y"),
        pd.to_datetime(d).strftime("%d.%m.%Y"),
        pd.to_datetime(d).strftime("%Y_%m_%d"),
        pd.to_datetime(d).strftime("%d/%m/%Y %H:%M"),
        d,
    ])
)


# ==================================================================
# ERROR 12: Silent decimal-slip
# ==================================================================
idx = np.random.choice(len(raw), 8, replace=False)
ucs_num = pd.to_numeric(raw["UCS"], errors="coerce")
ucs_num.loc[idx] = (ucs_num.loc[idx] * 10).round(2)
raw["UCS"] = ucs_num
print("Silent decimal-slip rows inserted: 8")


# ==================================================================
# ERROR 13: Patterned missing values
# ==================================================================
mask_labB = raw["Lab"] == "Lab-B"
for col in ["Water Content (%)", "P-wave Velocity (km/s)",
            "Brazilian Tensile (MPa)", "Is(50) (MPa)"]:
    raw.loc[mask_labB & (np.random.rand(len(raw)) < 0.35), col] = np.nan

mask_bh5 = raw["Borehole"] == "BH-05"
raw.loc[mask_bh5 & (np.random.rand(len(raw)) < 0.40), "Schmidt Rebound (R)"] = np.nan

for col in ["Porosity (%)", "Dry Density (g/cm3)"]:
    raw.loc[np.random.choice(len(raw), 22, replace=False), col] = np.nan


# ==================================================================
# Save to Excel + CSV
# ==================================================================
raw.to_excel("ucs_raw_dirty.xlsx", index=False, sheet_name="raw_data")
raw.to_csv("ucs_raw_dirty.csv", index=False)

print("\n✅ Saved: ucs_raw_dirty.xlsx + ucs_raw_dirty.csv")
print("Shape:", raw.shape)
print("\nFirst look:")
raw.head()

TASK 1: Data-Quality Audit

We audit the raw data without changing anything — only identify problems.

Audit plan:

  1. Text inside numeric columns
  2. Hidden placeholders (-777)
  3. Categorical spellings and mixed systems
  4. Duplicate rows and Sample IDs
  5. Missing values (after removing placeholders)
  6. Date formats

Audit 1: Text inside Numeric Columns

pd.to_numeric(errors="coerce") converts non-numeric values to NaN. We then display the original values that failed the conversion.

In [3]:

                "Porosity (%)", "Water Content (%)", "P-wave Velocity (km/s)",
                "Schmidt Rebound (R)", "Is(50) (MPa)", "Brazilian Tensile (MPa)", "UCS"]

print("=== AUDIT 1: Non-numeric values in numeric columns ===")
for c in numeric_cols:
    as_num = pd.to_numeric(raw[c], errors="coerce")
    bad = raw.loc[as_num.isna() & raw[c].notna(), c].unique()
    if len(bad):
        print(f"{c:28s} -> {list(bad)[:8]}")

TASK 2: Cleaning — Step by Step

Cleaning principles:

  1. Work on a copy of the raw data
  2. Fix one problem at a time
  3. Log every change
  4. Flag invalid tests instead of deleting them

Step 1: Setup & Change Log

df = raw.copy() preserves the original raw data. note() function records changes.

In [10]:
df = raw.copy()
log = []
def note(step, n):
    log.append({"step": step, "rows_affected": int(n)})
    print(f"✔ {step}: {n} rows affected")

Step 2: Standardise Column Names

Rename to snake_case for readability.

In [11]:

Step 3: Placeholders → NaN

Replace all placeholder tokens before numeric conversion.

In [12]:
before = df.isna().sum().sum()
df = df.replace(PLACEHOLDERS, np.nan)
df = df.replace(-777, np.nan)

# Object columns mein har cell ko safely string banao, phir strip karo
obj = [c for c in df.columns if not pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(df[c])]
for c in obj:
    df[c] = df[c].apply(lambda x: x.strip() if isinstance(x, str) else x)

df = df.replace("", np.nan)
note("Placeholders -> NaN (cells)", df.isna().sum().sum() - before)

✔ Placeholders -> NaN (cells): 51 rows affected

Step 4: Remove Conflicting Duplicates

Same Sample ID with different UCS → keep first, drop rest.

In [13]:
n0 = len(df)
df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=["sample_id"], keep="first")
note("Conflicting duplicates removed (kept first)", n0 - len(df))

Step 5: Clean Units from Text

Strip " mm" and " kg/m3" suffixes, then convert to numeric.

In [14]:
n_diam = df["diameter_mm"].astype(str).str.contains("mm", na=False).sum()
df["diameter_mm"] = df["diameter_mm"].astype(str).str.replace("mm","",regex=False).str.strip()

n_dens = df["dry_density"].astype(str).str.contains("kg/m3", na=False).sum()
df["dry_density"] = df["dry_density"].astype(str).str.replace("kg/m3","",regex=False).str.strip()

num = ["depth_m","diameter_mm","ld_ratio","dry_density","porosity",
       "water_content","vp_kms","schmidt_r","is50","bts","ucs"]
df[num] = df[num].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
note("Diameter ' mm' suffix cleaned", n_diam)
note("Density ' kg/m3' suffix cleaned", n_dens)

Step 6: Standardise Rock Type

6 rock types, 20+ spellings. Map all to standard names with a defensive assert.

In [15]:
def clean_rock(x):
    if pd.isna(x): return np.nan
    k = x.lower().replace("-","").replace(" ","").replace(".","")
    mapping = {
        "sandstone":"Sandstone", "ss":"Sandstone", "sandst":"Sandstone",
        "sandstn":"Sandstone",
        "limestone":"Limestone", "limestone":"Limestone", "ls":"Limestone",
        "limest":"Limestone",
        "shale":"Shale", "shl":"Shale", "sh":"Shale",
        "granite":"Granite", "gran":"Granite", "grnt":"Granite", "granit":"Granite",
        "mudstone":"Mudstone", "mdstone":"Mudstone", "mudst":"Mudstone",
        "basalt":"Basalt", "bslt":"Basalt", "bas":"Basalt", "baslt":"Basalt",
    }
    return mapping.get(k, "UNMAPPED:" + x)

old = df["rock_type"].copy()
df["rock_type"] = df["rock_type"].map(clean_rock)
note("Rock type labels corrected", (old != df["rock_type"]).sum())
assert not df["rock_type"].str.startswith("UNMAPPED").any()
df["rock_type"].value_counts()

Step 7: Standardise Weathering Grade

Three systems (Roman, numeric, descriptive) → one ISRM ordinal scale.

In [16]:
W_MAP = {
    "FRESH":"Fresh","F":"Fresh","GRADE-1":"Fresh","W1":"Fresh","FR":"Fresh",
    "SLIGHTLY WEATHERED":"Slightly Weathered","SW":"Slightly Weathered",
    "GRADE-2":"Slightly Weathered","W2":"Slightly Weathered",
    "SLGT-WTHRD":"Slightly Weathered",
    "MODERATELY WEATHERED":"Moderately Weathered","MW":"Moderately Weathered",
    "GRADE-3":"Moderately Weathered","W3":"Moderately Weathered",
    "HIGHLY WEATHERED":"Highly Weathered","HW":"Highly Weathered",
    "GRADE-4":"Highly Weathered","W4":"Highly Weathered",
    "COMPLETELY WEATHERED":"Completely Weathered","CW":"Completely Weathered",
    "GRADE-5":"Completely Weathered","W5":"Completely Weathered",
}
old = df["weathering"].copy()
df["weathering"] = df["weathering"].astype(str).str.upper().map(W_MAP)
note("Weathering codes standardised", (old != df["weathering"]).sum())

df["weathering"] = pd.Categorical(
    df["weathering"],
    categories=["Fresh","Slightly Weathered","Moderately Weathered",
                "Highly Weathered","Completely Weathered"],
    ordered=True)
df["weathering"].value_counts().sort_index()

Step 8: Convert UCS to MPa

The silent unit error — kPa/Pa values look normal but are 1,000× too large.

In [17]:

n_conv = (df["ucs_unit"] != "MPa").sum()
df["ucs"] = df["ucs"] * df["ucs_unit"].map(to_mpa)
df["ucs_unit"] = "MPa"
note("UCS converted to MPa", n_conv)
print("\nAFTER conversion:")
print(df["ucs"].describe().round(2))

Step 10: Physically Impossible Values

A value that breaks physics is an error, not an outlier. Set to NaN.

In [19]:
rules = {
    "depth_m":       (0, 200),
    "porosity":      (0, 60),
    "dry_density":   (1.2, 3.3),
    "ucs":           (0.1, 400),
    "schmidt_r":     (10, 70),
    "vp_kms":        (0.5, 7.5),
    "ld_ratio":      (1.0, 3.5),
    "diameter_mm":   (30, 150),
    "water_content": (0, 50),
}
for col, (lo, hi) in rules.items():
    bad = df[col].notna() & ~df[col].between(lo, hi)
    if bad.any():
        print(f"{col}: {bad.sum()} impossible values -> {df.loc[bad, col].round(1).tolist()[:6]}")
    df.loc[bad, col] = np.nan
    note(f"Out-of-range {col} set to NaN", bad.sum())

Step 11: Flag Invalid Tests

Two types: L/D > 3.0 and failure outside specimen body. Flag, don't delete.

In [20]:
df["valid_test"] = True

mask_ld = df["ld_ratio"] > 3.0
df.loc[mask_ld, "valid_test"] = False
note("Flagged invalid: L/D > 3.0", mask_ld.sum())

mask_fail = df["failure_mode"].eq("Failed outside specimen body")
df.loc[mask_fail, "valid_test"] = False
note("Flagged invalid: failed outside specimen body", mask_fail.sum())

print(df.groupby("valid_test")["ucs"].median().round(2))

Step 12: Parse Dates Explicitly

Avoid format="mixed" — try each known format explicitly.

In [21]:
shortcut = pd.to_datetime(df["test_date"], format="mixed", dayfirst=True, errors="coerce")

formats = ["%b-%d-%Y", "%d.%m.%Y", "%Y_%m_%d", "%d/%m/%Y %H:%M", "%Y-%m-%d"]
parsed = pd.Series(pd.NaT, index=df.index, dtype="datetime64[ns]")
for f in formats:
    parsed = parsed.fillna(pd.to_datetime(df["test_date"], format=f, errors="coerce"))

print("Dates the shortcut got WRONG:", (shortcut != parsed).sum())
df["test_date"] = parsed
note("Unparseable dates", df["test_date"].isna().sum())
df["test_date"].agg(["min","max"])

Step 13: Outlier Detection

Statistical outlier ≠ error. Cross-check with k = UCS / Is(50) — normally 10–30.

In [22]:
def iqr_flag(s, k=1.5):
    q1, q3 = s.quantile([.25, .75]); iqr = q3 - q1
    return ~s.between(q1 - k*iqr, q3 + k*iqr)

df["ucs_outlier_iqr"] = df.groupby("rock_type")["ucs"].transform(iqr_flag) & df["ucs"].notna()
df["ucs_schmidt_ratio"] = df["ucs"] / df["schmidt_r"]
df["ucs_suspect"] = df["ucs_schmidt_ratio"].notna() & (df["ucs_schmidt_ratio"] > 8)
note("Suspicious UCS/Schmidt-R ratio flagged", df["ucs_suspect"].sum())
print(df.loc[df["ucs_suspect"],
             ["sample_id","rock_type","weathering","ucs","schmidt_r","ucs_schmidt_ratio"]]
        .sort_values("ucs_schmidt_ratio", ascending=False).round(2).head(8))

✔ Suspicious UCS/Schmidt-R ratio flagged: 0 rows affected

Step 14: Handle Missing Values

Target missing → drop. Predictors → group median (rock type + weathering).

In [23]:
n0 = len(df)
df = df.dropna(subset=["ucs"])
note("Rows dropped: missing UCS (target)", n0 - len(df))

impute_cols = ["depth_m","dry_density","porosity","water_content",
               "vp_kms","schmidt_r","is50","bts"]
for c in impute_cols:
    df[f"{c}_was_missing"] = df[c].isna()
    grp_med = df.groupby(["rock_type","weathering"], observed=True)[c].transform("median")
    df[c] = df[c].fillna(grp_med).fillna(df.groupby("rock_type")[c].transform("median"))
    note(f"Imputed {c}", df[f"{c}_was_missing"].sum())

df["moisture"] = df["moisture"].fillna("Unknown")
df["failure_mode"] = df["failure_mode"].fillna("Not recorded")

TASK 3: Exploratory Data Analysis

Now that the data is clean, we explore:

  • Summary statistics
  • Pie charts for categorical distributions
  • UCS distribution (log scale)
  • Rock type and weathering comparisons
  • Spearman correlation
  • k-fit per rock type
  • Moisture confounding control
  • Depth vs weathering
  • ISRM classification
  • Raw vs clean comparison

    a.set_xlabel(lab, fontsize=11)
    a.set_ylabel("UCS (MPa)", fontsize=11)
    rho = stats.spearmanr(clean[x], clean["ucs"]).statistic
    a.set_title(f"UCS vs {lab}   (ρ = {rho:.2f})", fontsize=11)

In [36]:
rows = []
for rt, g in clean[~clean["is50_was_missing"]].groupby("rock_type"):
    k = (g["ucs"] * g["is50"]).sum() / (g["is50"] ** 2).sum()
    pred = k * g["is50"]
    r2 = 1 - ((g["ucs"] - pred) ** 2).sum() / ((g["ucs"] - g["ucs"].mean()) ** 2).sum()
    rows.append({"rock_type": rt, "n": len(g),
                 "k (UCS/Is50)": round(k, 1), "R2": round(r2, 2)})
kfit = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("rock_type").loc[order]
kfit

REPORT: Findings & Discussion

Summary

Task 1 — Data-Quality Audit
13 types of problems identified. Worst silent errors: kPa/Pa unit mixing, decimal slips, day/month swaps, invalid failure modes.

Task 2 — Cleaning
Every change logged; invalid tests flagged, not deleted. Final dataset saved as ucs_clean.csv.

Task 3 — EDA
Rock type and weathering grade are the main controls on UCS. Weathering alone can reduce strength by more than 90%. Is(50) and BTS are the best predictors (ρ ≈ 0.97). Fitted k values fall in the published range (10–30). Saturation weakens shale and mudstone most. The apparent depth trend is mostly a weathering effect.

Conclusion

A systematic data-cleaning workflow converted a deliberately corrupted dataset into an analysis-ready form. The cleaned dataset revealed physically sensible relationships between UCS, rock type, weathering, and index tests.

Key lesson: data cleaning is not optional — silent errors make any downstream analysis meaningless.

Next step: build a predictive model: log(UCS) from Is(50), Vp, Schmidt R, porosity, rock type, and weathering — cross-validated by borehole.
